answer: Each identity registers one meadow apiary: it locks a 70-credit bond, paints its hive boxes umber, seals each box with an opal tag bound to its key, and publishes the hive count on a public ledger. An auditor recounts the tagged boxes each epoch; a count mismatch or reused tag burns the bond. The k-th apiary pays 26+5(k-1) credits, so the 1000th pays 5021 and 1000 fakes pay 2,523,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-hive ring fails because tags carry the renter's key, and the recount exposes duplicates. An honest keeper pays 26 once and recovers the 70 bond when clean.
